lesson_title: The Envelope That Shrinks: Deductions, Contributions and the Payroll
hook_text: You earned R8 800. You received R6 442. Nobody stole a cent.
clip_script: Imagine payday as an envelope with your name on it. Inside: everything you earned — R8 800. But between the safe and your hands, it makes five stops. The tax man: R1 100. Your retirement jar: R660 — a letter to your future self. Just-in-case insurance: R88. Doctor cover: R450. The union — your collective voice: R60. The envelope lands holding R6 442. Here's the part that changes how you read every payslip forever: nothing was taken FROM you. Every rand that left was YOUR money, sent ahead to places you agreed it should go. And there's a second envelope you never see — the boss matching your pension rand for rand, matching your insurance, paying a skills levy — R1 286 more, on top. Your job really costs R10 086 a month. Two envelopes. Keep them apart, and payroll is just addition.
visual_style: An envelope travelling a conveyor past five glowing stations, coins hopping out at each; then a second, translucent envelope materialising beside it and both pouring into a final total.
pacing: Rhythmic per-stop beats, a pause on 'nothing was taken FROM you', building to the two-envelope reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read your first payslip like an accountant.
